about: AL Planner OFFLINE GURU knowledge bank — Sri Lankan G.C.E. A/L syllabus (2019+) quick-expert answers. Works with zero API key / internet. Each topic: keys (match words), subj, title, body (plain text, bullet lines).

topics.title: The mole concept
topics.body:
1 mole = 6.022×10²³ particles (Avogadro constant).
• n = m / M   (mass ÷ molar mass)
• n = C × V in dm³  (divide cm³ by 1000)
• Gases at r.t.p.: V = n × 24.0 dm³
Exam tip: always convert every quantity to moles FIRST, then use the equation ratio.

topics.title: Titration calculations
topics.body:
Steps: 1) moles of KNOWN = C × V/1000  2) use the equation ratio  3) C = n × 1000 / V.
Example: 25.00 cm³ NaOH vs 0.1000 mol dm⁻³ HCl, mean titre 24.00 cm³ (1:1):
C(NaOH) = 0.1000 × 24.00 / 25.00 = 0.0960 mol dm⁻³.
Only average CONCORDANT titres (±0.10 cm³); the rough titre is never averaged.
Try it live: Lab → 🧪 Practical Lab → Titration.

topics.title: pH & pOH
topics.body:
pH = −log₁₀[H⁺];  pOH = −log₁₀[OH⁻];  pH + pOH = 14.00 at 25 °C.
Strong acid fully ionises: 0.1 mol dm⁻³ HCl → pH 1. Weak acids give HIGHER pH at the same concentration.
Diluting a strong acid 10× raises pH by exactly 1.

topics.title: Choosing indicators
topics.body:
Methyl orange: red < 3.1 → yellow > 4.4. Phenolphthalein: colourless < 8.3 → pink > 10.
Strong acid + strong base → either. Strong acid + weak base → methyl orange. Weak acid + strong base → phenolphthalein. Weak + weak → no indicator works; use a pH meter.
Indicators are weak acids: HIn ⇌ H⁺ + In⁻, the two forms have different colours.

topics.title: Le Chatelier & Kc
topics.body:
A system at equilibrium opposes any change: add reactant → shifts right; add heat → shifts endothermic way; raise pressure → shifts to fewer gas moles.
Kc changes ONLY with temperature — never with concentration, pressure or a catalyst. A catalyst only reaches equilibrium faster.
Haber: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ (ΔH −): high P, moderate T, remove NH₃.
Try it: Lab → Simulator Library → Equilibrium & Le Chatelier (or the 🌡️ practical).

topics.title: Flame tests
topics.body:
Na⁺ golden-yellow (persistent) · K⁺ lilac · Ca²⁺ brick-red · Sr²⁺/Li⁺ crimson red · Ba²⁺ apple-green · Cu²⁺ blue-green.
Why: heat excites electrons; each drop emits light of one energy (E = hν) → element's line spectrum. It is PHYSICAL, not burning.
Clean the wire in conc. HCl first — trace Na⁺ masks everything. Try it: 🧪 Practical Lab → Flame Tests.

topics.title: Precipitate / ion tests
topics.body:
Cl⁻ → AgNO₃: white AgCl, dissolves in dilute NH₃, insoluble in dilute HNO₃. Br⁻ cream (AgBr), I⁻ yellow (AgI, insoluble even in conc. NH₃).
SO₄²⁻ → BaCl₂: white BaSO₄, ACID-INSOLUBLE. CO₃²⁻ → BaCl₂: white BaCO₃ that fizzes away in acid.
NaOH dropwise→excess: Cu²⁺ blue ppt (excess NH₃ → deep blue complex) · Fe²⁺ dirty-green ppt · Fe³⁺ red-brown ppt · Al³⁺/Zn²⁺ white, dissolve in excess NaOH; only Zn²⁺ dissolves in excess NH₃.
Practise: 🧪 Practical Lab → Precipitation / UNKNOWN challenge.

topics.title: Ionic equations
topics.body:
1) Write the balanced molecular equation. 2) Split strong electrolytes (soluble salts, strong acids/bases) into ions. 3) Cancel SPECTATOR ions appearing unchanged on both sides. 4) Check atoms AND total charge balance.
Example: AgNO₃ + NaCl → AgCl(s) + NaNO₃ becomes Ag⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq) → AgCl(s).

topics.title: Redox & oxidation numbers
topics.body:
OIL RIG: Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain of electrons. Oxidation numbers: free element 0; O usually −2 (peroxide −1); H +1 (metal hydrides −1); sum = charge.
Acid KMnO₄: Mn +7 → +2 (purple → colourless). Acid K₂Cr₂O₇: Cr +6 → +3 (orange → green).
Balance in acid: O with H₂O, H with H⁺, charge with e⁻; electrons must cancel in the overall equation.

topics.title: Organic identification tests
topics.body:
C=C: decolourises orange bromine water instantly (addition); also decolourises KMnO₄.
Aldehyde: Fehling's → brick-red Cu₂O; Tollens' → silver mirror. Ketone: NEITHER (but both give orange ppt with 2,4-DNP → proves C=O).
Carboxylic acid: fizzes CO₂ with Na₂CO₃. Primary alcohols: acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ orange → green on warming.

topics.title: Galvanic cells
topics.body:
Lower E° metal = ANODE (−): oxidation, dissolves. Higher E° = CATHODE (+): reduction, metal deposits.
E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode. Daniell: 0.34 −(−0.76) = 1.10 V. Electrons flow anode→cathode through the WIRE; ions migrate through the salt bridge (cations toward cathode).
Try it: 🧪 Practical Lab → Electrochemical Cells.

topics.title: Rates & collision theory
topics.body:
Rate rises with concentration(pressure), temperature, surface area, and catalysts.
Particle reason: MORE frequent EFFECTIVE collisions; T mainly increases collision ENERGY (more exceed Ea); a catalyst gives a lower-Ea path.
Catalyst ≠ more product — same final amount, faster. Rate at time t = gradient of the volume–time curve.

topics.title: Electrolysis
topics.body:
Anode (+) = oxidation; cathode (−) = reduction — opposite signs to a galvanic cell!
Molten NaCl: Na at cathode, Cl₂ at anode. Aqueous: compare discharge (reactivity vs concentration).
Q = I × t (coulombs); 1 mol e⁻ = 96,500 C. Mass deposited ∝ charge.

topics.title: Gas laws
topics.body:
Boyle: pV = constant (fixed T). Charles: V/T = constant (fixed p). Combined: p₁V₁/T₁ = p₂V₂/T₂.
Ideal gas: pV = nRT (R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, T in KELVIN).
Real gases deviate at high p / low T. Try it: Lab → Gas Laws simulator.

topics.title: Solubility & crystallisation
topics.body:
Solubility = max grams of solute per 100 g water at a stated temperature (saturated solution).
Most solid salts dissolve MORE when hot → heat, saturate, then cool slowly: excess leaves as crystals.
Example KNO₃ ~64 g/100 g at 40 °C but ~32 g at 20 °C. Slow cooling = big crystals. Try it: 🧪 Practical Lab → Solubility.

topics.title: Atomic structure & configuration
topics.body:
Isotopes: same protons, different neutrons.
Fill orbitals by energy: 1s 2s 2p 3s 3p 4s 3d 4p (max 2/6/10/14).
Example Fe (Z=26): 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁶4s²3d⁶. Ions: remove 4s FIRST → Fe²⁺ = [Ar]3d⁶.
Blocks d/f give transition/f-block behaviour (coloured ions, catalysis).

topics.title: Chemical bonding & shapes
topics.body:
Ionic: full transfer (metal + non-metal) — high m.p., conduct when molten/aqueous. Covalent: sharing; H-bonds explain water's high b.p. and clustering.
VSEPR: electron pairs repel to maximum separation. 4 pairs → tetrahedral (CH₄ 109.5°); lone pairs compress: NH₃ 107°, H₂O 104.5°; CO₂ linear 180°.
Try it: Lab → VSEPR / Polarity simulators.

topics.title: Periodic table quick facts
topics.body:
Group 1 alkali metals: reactivity increases DOWN (easier e⁻ loss). Group 17 halogens: reactivity increases UP (easier e⁻ gain); a higher halogen displaces a lower one.
Group 18 noble gases: full outer shell — inert. Try it: Lab → Periodic Table simulator.

topics.title: Projectile motion
topics.body:
Split into components: horizontal velocity constant (u cosθ); vertical accelerates at g.
Time of flight T = 2u sinθ/g; range R = u² sin2θ/g (max at 45°); max height H = u²sin²θ/2g.
Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² unless told otherwise. Try it: Lab → Projectile simulator.

topics.title: Equations of motion
topics.body:
v = u + at · s = ut + ½at² · v² = u² + 2as · s = ½(u+v)t.
Valid only for CONSTANT acceleration. Write u, v, a, s, t; find the 3 you know; pick the equation containing the missing one. Signs matter (choose a positive direction!).

topics.title: Newton's laws
topics.body:
1st: no NET force → no change in motion (inertia). 2nd: F(net) = ma — resultant force, not just any force. 3rd: equal-opposite pairs act on DIFFERENT bodies.
Weight = mg acts on you; the 3rd-law pair acts on the Earth. Lift problems: scale reads m(g±a).

topics.title: Work, energy, power
topics.body:
W = F s cosθ. KE = ½mv²; GPE = mgh; conservation: KE + PE constant when only gravity works.
Work–energy theorem: net work = ΔKE. Power = W/t = Fv.
Try it: Lab → Work–Energy simulator.

topics.title: Simple harmonic motion
topics.body:
a = −ω²x (acceleration toward the centre, ∝ displacement). x = A sin(ωt); vmax = ωA; amax = ω²A.
Pendulum: T = 2π√(l/g). Spring: T = 2π√(m/k). T independent of amplitude (isochronous). Try it: Lab → SHM simulator.

topics.title: Waves
topics.body:
v = fλ. Transverse (light, strings): oscillation ⊥ travel. Longitudinal (sound): parallel.
Superposition: crest+crest = bigger (constructive), crest+trough = cancel (destructive). Stationary waves on strings: nodes/antinodes; fundamental = λ/2 string length. Try it: Lab → Waves & Sound simulators.

topics.title: Circuits: Ohm & Kirchhoff
topics.body:
V = IR. Series: current same, Rs add. Parallel: voltage same, 1/Rp = Σ1/R.
Kirchhoff 1 (junction): currents in = out (charge conserved). Kirchhoff 2 (loop): emf sum = p.d. sum (energy conserved).
Energy: P = VI = I²R = V²/R. Try it: Lab → Circuits / Ohm's Law / Circuit Builder.

topics.title: Optics
topics.body:
Snell: n₁ sinθ₁ = n₂ sinθ₂; critical angle sinC = 1/n (into air) → total internal reflection beyond C.
Lens/mirror: 1/f = 1/u + 1/v (real-is-positive convention); magnification m = v/u.
Convex: f>0; concave: f<0. Try it: Lab → Optics / Refraction / Lens & Mirror Bench.

topics.title: Moments & equilibrium
topics.body:
Moment = force × perpendicular distance. A body in equilibrium: ΣF = 0 AND Σmoments = 0 about any point.
Stable equilibrium: centre of gravity rises when tilted, so it falls back.

topics.title: Differentiation
topics.body:
d/dx xⁿ = n xⁿ⁻¹. Product: (uv)' = u'v + uv'. Quotient: (u/v)' = (u'v − uv')/v². Chain: dy/dx = dy/du × du/dx.
Uses: gradient of tangent; stationary points where dy/dx = 0 (test sign change for max/min); rate of change.
Try it: Lab → Derivative explorer.

topics.title: Integration
topics.body:
∫xⁿ dx = xⁿ⁺¹/(n+1) + C (n ≠ −1). Reverse of differentiation.
Definite integral = signed area under the curve: subtract below-axis parts for total area.
∫(ax+b)ⁿ dx = (ax+b)ⁿ⁺¹ / a(n+1) + C. Try it: Lab → Integration explorer.

topics.title: Trig you must know
topics.body:
sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; tanθ = sinθ/cosθ; sin2θ = 2 sinθ cosθ; cos2θ = 2cos²θ −1 = 1−2sin²θ.
Sine rule: a/sinA = b/sinB. Cosine rule: a² = b² + c² − 2bc cosA.
Angles in RADIANS for calculus. Try it: Lab → Trig simulator.

topics.title: Vectors
topics.body:
|a| = √(x² + y²). Dot product: a·b = |a||b|cosθ = x₁x₂ + y₁y₂ → find angles; a·b = 0 ⇔ perpendicular.
Resultant: add components. Unit vector = a/|a|. Try it: Lab → Vector playground.

topics.title: Quadratics
topics.body:
Roots: x = (−b ± √(b²−4ac)) / 2a. Discriminant: >0 two real, =0 equal, <0 no real roots.
Sum = −b/a, product = c/a. Vertex at x = −b/2a; completing the square for min/max.

topics.title: AP & GP
topics.body:
AP: Tn = a + (n−1)d; Sn = n/2 (2a + (n−1)d).
GP: Tn = a rⁿ⁻¹; Sn = a(rⁿ−1)/(r−1); |r|<1 gives S∞ = a/(1−r).
Find a and d (or r) from two given terms first.

topics.title: Probability
topics.body:
P(A∪B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A∩B). Independent: P(A∩B) = P(A)P(B). Mutually exclusive: P(A∩B) = 0.
Complement: P(A′) = 1 − P(A) — great for 'at least one' questions.
Permutations n!, combinations ⁿCᵣ = n!/(r!(n−r)!). Try it: Lab → Probability lab.

topics.title: Coordinate geometry basics
topics.body:
y = mx + c; gradient m = (y₂−y₁)/(x₂−x₁). Parallel: m₁ = m₂. Perpendicular: m₁m₂ = −1.
Distance = √((Δx)²+(Δy)²); midpoint = averages. Try it: Lab → Graph plotter & transformations.

topics.title: Cell organelles
topics.body:
Nucleus: DNA/control. Mitochondria: aerobic respiration → ATP. Ribosomes: protein synthesis. RER+ribosomes: export proteins; Golgi: modifies/packages. Chloroplast: photosynthesis. Lysosome: digestion.
Plant extras: cell wall (cellulose), large central vacuole, chloroplasts. Prokaryotes: no nucleus, 70S ribosomes.

topics.title: Photosynthesis
topics.body:
6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ (light + chlorophyll).
Light stage (thylakoids): water splits → O₂; ATP + NADPH made. Calvin cycle (stroma): CO₂ fixed (RuBP) → reduced to sugar using ATP/NADPH.
Limiting factors: light, CO₂, temperature. Try it: Lab → Photosynthesis simulator.

topics.title: Respiration
topics.body:
Aerobic: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + ATP (~30–32 per glucose).
Glycolysis (cytoplasm) → link + Krebs (matrix) → electron transport (cristae, most ATP).
Anaerobic (muscles): lactate (+little ATP); yeast: ethanol + CO₂. Try it: Lab → Cellular Respiration map.

topics.title: Enzymes
topics.body:
Protein catalysts; substrate fits the active site (induced fit).
Rate rises with temperature until the optimum, then falls — bonds break, active site lost = DENATURATION (permanent). pH likewise has an optimum.
Km = substrate level at half Vmax; low Km = high affinity. Try it: Lab → Enzyme Kinetics.

topics.title: Heart & double circulation
topics.body:
Right side: deoxygenated blood to lungs; left side: oxygenated blood to body — left ventricle wall is THICKEST (longest push).
Valves stop backflow: atrioventricular + semilunar.
Sequence: atria contract → ventricles contract → both relax. Try it: Lab → Heart simulator.

topics.title: DNA & protein synthesis
topics.body:
Double helix; A–T (2 H-bonds), G–C (3). Replication is SEMI-conservative: each new molecule keeps one old strand.
Transcription (nucleus): DNA → mRNA. Translation (ribosome): mRNA codons → amino acids via tRNA.
1 codon = 3 bases = 1 amino acid. Try it: Lab → DNA simulator.

topics.title: Transpiration
topics.body:
Loss of water vapour mostly through stomata; pulled up by cohesion–tension in xylem.
Faster with: more light (stomata open), heat, wind, LOW humidity. Benefits: water/mineral transport + cooling; danger: wilting.

topics.title: Number systems
topics.body:
Binary↔decimal: 1101₂ = 8+4+0+1 = 13. Decimal→binary: repeated ÷2 remainders.
Hex: 4 bits per digit — A = 1010 = 10, F = 1111 = 15.
2's complement flips bits +1 → used for negative integers. 1 byte = 8 bits. Try it: Lab → Binary workshop.

topics.title: Logic gates
topics.body:
AND: 1 only when all 1. OR: 1 if any 1. NOT: inverts. NAND = AND+NOT (universal). XOR: 1 when inputs DIFFER.
Half adder = XOR (sum) + AND (carry). Draw the truth table row by row for any circuit. Try it: Lab → Logic gates / Truth tables.

topics.title: Networks & IP
topics.body:
LAN = one site; WAN = cities/countries. OSI 7 layers vs TCP/IP 4.
IPv4 = 32 bits, 4 octets. Classes: A (1–126, /8), B (128–191, /16), C (192–223, /24). Private ranges: 10.0.0.0/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16. Subnet mask splits network vs host bits.
Try it: Lab → IP Addressing & Networks.

topics.title: Databases & SQL
topics.body:
Primary key: unique, not null. Foreign key: links tables.
SELECT cols FROM t WHERE cond ORDER BY col LIMIT n.
Normalisation: 1NF atomic values; 2NF no partial dependency; 3NF no transitive dependency — removes update/insert/delete anomalies.
Try it: Lab → SQL playground.

topics.title: SDLC
topics.body:
Phases: feasibility → analysis → design → implementation → testing → deployment → maintenance.
Waterfall: strict sequence, easy to manage, weak when requirements change. Agile/iterative: small cycles, user feedback each round — better for evolving requirements.
